post.summary: Settle a security deposit after move-out
post.description:
Security deposit settlement for a US rental under the state's statute (and a covered city's ordinance): the date to return the deposit and itemized statement, each intended deduction assessed (allowed or not, prorated by useful life, documentation needed), interest owed, refund due, penalty exposure, a draft itemized statement and a citation for every rule. Covers all 50 states and DC, with city overlays for Chicago, San Francisco, Berkeley, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Minneapolis and Saint Paul.
When to use: A landlord or property manager is closing a move-out and asks when the deposit must be returned, what they may deduct (carpet, paint, cleaning, unpaid rent), how much interest is owed, what to put in the itemized statement, or what happens if they are late.
Not for: Not legal advice and not a tenant demand letter. It does not price repairs (use property_turnover_quick_estimate for that), hold or account for deposits, or cover pet deposits, last-month's rent handling or non-US rentals. Where the statute sets no deadline (Kentucky, Tennessee) it says so; never present a guessed date as the rule.
Tip: Send as_of (today's date) for a repeatable answer; it defaults to today in UTC.
Tip: Give item_installed_on or item_age_years for carpet, paint, blinds and appliances; without them the tenancy length is assumed.
Tip: Mark normal wear with caused_by_tenant false; it is never deductible.
Tip: Relay deadline.return_by and its status, totals.refund_due_usd, penalty_exposure and the citations; say it is not legal advice.
Tip: Offer statement.text as the draft itemized statement; it has no names or addresses.
Tip: Relay warnings, assumptions and unknowns (for example the Texas forwarding address).
Tip: Send the start-event dates a state needs when known (forwarding_address_received_on, demand_received_on, new_tenant_moved_in_on, claim_notice_sent_on in Florida); without them the clock is not_started.
Tip: deadline.status none_in_statute means no statutory deadline; deadline.extended_to is the statute's weekend roll-forward, but advise acting by return_by.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability deposit-settlement v0.1.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Security deposit rules for a state (and city)
post.description:
The security deposit rules for one US state, with a covered city's overlay: return deadline and what starts it, itemization and documentation duties, allowed deductions and depreciation, interest, penalty, deposit cap and recent changes, with citations.
When to use: Someone asks what a state's (or a covered city's) security deposit rules are without a specific move-out to settle, or which states are covered.
Not for: To settle a specific deposit (use deposit_settlement_settle, which applies the rules to the dates and deductions). Other landlord-tenant topics (evictions, rent control, notice periods) are not covered.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability deposit-settlement v0.1.0 (experimental).

The easiest way to estimate a US rental turnover: a ZIP, bedrooms, bathrooms and a list of plain-English issues in, a priced make-ready estimate out (same engine and result as property_turnover_scope, short summary by default).
When to use: Start here when the user describes a move-out or turnover in words ("carpet stained in both bedrooms, oven filthy") and wants a cost estimate or what to tell vendors. Use property_turnover_scope instead for rate cards, owner decisions, measured quantities or per-finding control.
Not for: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
Tip: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Tip: Relay refer_outs first, then the totals; say the numbers are estimates, not quotes.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v0.3.0 (experimental).

Turn move-out / turnover inspection findings for a US rental unit into a priced make-ready scope: standardized tasks by trade, regional low/expected/high costs, must/should/could priorities, vendor scopes, refer-outs to licensed professionals, and every assumption stated.
When to use: Turnover findings for a US rental unit when you need control: rooms, measured quantities, the manager's own prices (rate_card) or owner approve/decline decisions. For a plain-English estimate, property_turnover_quick_estimate is easier.
Not for: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
Tip: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Tip: Describe each finding in plain words (description). Only send a code returned by property_turnover_issue_codes; unmatched findings come back as manual-quote lines with suggested codes.
Tip: Give measured quantities when you have them (e.g. 120 sq_ft); otherwise typical sizes are assumed and listed in assumptions.
Tip: Send property.floor_coverings when you know whether there is carpet, and unit_type single_family for houses; both change the baseline scope.
Tip: Relay the summary, refer_outs, assumptions and unknowns to the user; costs are estimate ranges, not quotes.
Tip: Use detail=summary unless the user asks for every line item (summary already lists every line tied to a finding).
Tip: Rate card examples - {"trade": "handyman", "unit_price": 65, "uom": "hour"} or {"task_id": "carpet.clean", "unit_price": 0.2, "uom": "sq_ft"}; check rate_card_applied and rate_card_ignored before saying a rate was used.
Tip: For the Excel workbook or owner estimate, give the user links.web_tool_prefilled (opens the free web tool with these findings) or POST the same arguments to links.downloads; do not build a spreadsheet yourself.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v0.3.0 (experimental).

Search the standard taxonomy of rental-unit turnover issues (component.issue codes) by keyword or area.
When to use: Only while preparing findings for a turnover cost estimate, to find the standard issue code for something observed (e.g. "pet stain on carpet"). Never needed to answer a question; call with no arguments to list the taxonomy areas and the first codes.
Not for: Legal or security-deposit questions; anything outside rental turnover and make-ready work. Not needed before quick_estimate or scope: a plain description works there.
Tip: Call with no arguments to list the taxonomy areas (in `areas`) and the first codes.
Tip: Codes are optional for scoping; a plain description also works.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v0.3.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Settle a security deposit after move-out (paid)
post.description: Paid lane (x402 v2, exact scheme, USDC on Base Sepolia testnet, $0.02 per call). Same body as POST /v1/deposit-settlement/settle, which stays free within its rate limits. Unpaid requests get HTTP 402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED; only successful results are charged. Not available over MCP. The response adds `payment` (network, transaction, payer).

402.description: Payment required (x402 v2). The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the base64 payment requirements; retry with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. Also returned for an invalid payment or a failed settlement (nothing charged).

422.description: Invalid input. Checked before payment; never charged.

429.description: Rate limited (per payer wallet or per client). Never charged.

get.description:
Aggregate settlement counts for the configured network: by payer class and route,
external payers and revenue, and ``qualified_repeat_demand`` (at least 5 external
wallets with at least 5 settled calls each). No wallet addresses; refreshed every few
minutes.

post.summary: Send feedback about the site, a tool, or an idea for a new tool
post.description: Free text plus a scope. For humans (the web forms use it); there is no MCP tool for this on purpose. Messages are capped at 2000 characters, links are replaced with [link] and at most 3 are accepted. Provide an email only if you want a reply. Rate limited to 5 per minute. Leave `website` empty.

Alternative.title: Alternative
Alternative.description:
A different deadline when a condition holds (e.g. 14 days when nothing is deducted).

``condition`` is the statute's case in words. The engine evaluates it when ``requires``
lists mapped conditions, when the condition itself is one (``no_deductions``), or when an
effective-date window is the whole condition; any other alternative keeps the base rule and
adds an assumption naming it. ``combine`` says how a matching alternative applies:
``replace`` the base period (the first match wins), or take the ``later_date`` /
``earlier_date`` of the base deadline and this one (Connecticut: 21 days after the end of
the tenancy or 15 days after the forwarding address, whichever is later).

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: What the citation supports: deadline, interest, penalty, ...

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Short quote of the rule (or our summary when verbatim is false).

CostRange.title: CostRange
CostRange.description: A low / expected / high estimate. Invariant: low <= expected <= high.

return_by.title: Return By
return_by.description: Last day to return the deposit.

itemization_by.title: Itemization By
itemization_by.description: Last day for the itemized statement (often the same day; earlier in Chicago, later in Louisiana).

extended_to.title: Extended To
extended_to.description: Where the state's code rolls a last day on a weekend or holiday to the next business day: that later date. Act by return_by; this is the legal outer limit.

start_event.title: Start Event
start_event.description: What starts the clock, in words.

days.title: Days
days.description: Period in days (None: months or none).

months.title: Months
months.description: Period in calendar months, if any.

status.title: Status
status.description: upcoming, due_today, overdue; not_started when the start event is not given yet; none_in_statute when the statute sets no deadline (Kentucky, Tennessee).

days_remaining.title: Days Remaining
days_remaining.description: Days from as_of to return_by (negative when overdue).

Decision.title: Decision
Decision.description: Owner decision. Re-run the same request with decisions to get the approved scope.

category.title: Category
category.description: One of: unpaid_rent, unpaid_utilities, cleaning, carpet, flooring, paint, blinds_window_coverings, appliance, fixture_or_hardware, wall_or_door_repair, key_or_lock, late_fees, lease_break_fee, other_damage, other.

description.title: Description
description.description: Your own short note (e.g. 'bedroom carpet, pet stains'). Never stored, hashed or returned; the statement uses the category.

amount_usd.title: Amount Usd
amount_usd.description: Amount you intend to deduct, in dollars (rounded to cents).

item_installed_on.title: Item Installed On
item_installed_on.description: When the item (carpet, paint, appliance...) was installed or last replaced (YYYY-MM-DD). Give this or item_age_years, not both.

item_age_years.title: Item Age Years
item_age_years.description: Age of the item in years at move-out (e.g. 4.5).

useful_life_years.title: Useful Life Years
useful_life_years.description: Override the useful life used for depreciation (years).

caused_by_tenant.title: Caused By Tenant
caused_by_tenant.description: False when the condition is normal wear and tear (never deductible).

has_receipt.title: Has Receipt
has_receipt.description: You have a receipt, invoice or estimate for this line.

has_photos.title: Has Photos
has_photos.description: You have photos of this damage.

amount_allowed_usd.title: Amount Allowed Usd
amount_allowed_usd.description: What the rule lets you keep for this line ('depends' lines: not counted in totals until you confirm).

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: Other caps by tenancy type or term; checked against the main.

method.title: Method
method.description: straight_line: max(0, 1 - age / useful life); step_table: the band of a published schedule for the item's age (California paint).

age_years.title: Age Years
age_years.description: Age at move-out: full calendar years plus remaining days / 365, 2 decimals.

remaining_fraction.title: Remaining Fraction
remaining_fraction.description: Share of the cost the tenant can be charged, 4 decimals.

source.title: Source
source.description: useful_life row id (row:jurisdiction for a variant) or 'request'.

schedule_source.title: Schedule Source
schedule_source.description: Source id of the step table, when one was used.

itemized_statement.title: Itemized Statement
itemized_statement.description: You will send (or sent) an itemized statement.

receipts.title: Receipts
receipts.description: You have receipts or invoices for the repairs and cleaning.

EstimateContext.title: EstimateContext
EstimateContext.description:
Identifiers of the estimate being rated. Hashes, versions, region and total only.

Every field has a strict format (security review M1): they end up in the feedback digest,
so nothing here may carry free text.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: site, a specific tool, or an idea for a new tool.

capability.title: Capability
capability.description: Tool id when scope is tool.

page.title: Page
page.description: Path of the page the feedback is about.

email.title: Email
email.description: Only if you want a reply.

FeedbackIn.title: FeedbackIn
FeedbackIn.description: What the site, a tool or an idea box sends to ``POST /v1/feedback``.

id.title: Id
id.description: Your id for this finding; defaults to f1, f2, ... in order.

location.description: Object {"area": "bedroom", "label": "Bedroom 2"}, or a plain string such as "Bedroom 2" or "kitchen" (mapped to an area; other text becomes the label).

code.title: Code
code.description: Optional. Only a code returned by property_turnover_issue_codes (e.g. 'walls.nail_holes'); otherwise leave it out and use description.

description.title: Description
description.description: Plain description if no code, e.g. 'dog urine stains in bedroom carpet'.

extent.description: spot | partial | full; defaults per issue.

quantity.description: Measured amount, e.g. 120 sq_ft. Derived when omitted.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description: One observed condition. Give a taxonomy `code` if you know it, else a `description`.

text.title: Text
text.description: The finding as given (description, else code), for tracing.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where, as shown on the lines.

match_note.title: Match Note
match_note.description: Set when the match left a fixture word unexplained: check this finding.

uncertain.title: Uncertain
uncertain.description: The description hedges ('mold?', 'maybe', 'possible'). Refer-outs from uncertain findings are check-first: they add a warning instead of holding phases.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.description: Suggested codes with readable names, best first.

carpet_present.title: Carpet Present
carpet_present.description: Is there wall-to-wall carpet? Omit if unknown: carpet findings then imply carpet; with no carpet findings, whole-unit carpet cleaning is left out and listed as unknown.

carpet_sq_ft.title: Carpet Sq Ft
carpet_sq_ft.description: Carpeted floor area. Omit to assume 60% of the unit floor area.

FloorCoverings.title: FloorCoverings
FloorCoverings.description: What is on the floors. Drives the carpet-cleaning baseline and whole-unit carpet sizes.

required.title: Required
required.description: None: depends on facts you did not give.

rate_percent.title: Rate Percent
rate_percent.description: Percent per year (the move-out rate when rates change).

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: What the rate applies to: deposit, or the excess (Ohio).

base_usd.title: Base Usd
base_usd.description: The amount the rate applies to.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: Per-period amounts when the rate changed.

InterestPart.title: InterestPart
InterestPart.description: One period of an interest computation at one rate (a year, a rate window).

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

query.title: Query
query.description: Keywords to match against codes, names and aliases, e.g. 'pet stain carpet'.

area.title: Area
area.description: Optional taxonomy area filter, e.g. 'flooring' or 'walls' (not a room). Call with no arguments to list every area in `areas`.

include_aliases.title: Include Aliases
include_aliases.description: Also return each code's aliases (larger result).

areas.title: Areas
areas.description: Every taxonomy area, for the `area` filter (e.g. 'flooring', 'walls').

city.title: City
city.description: The city you sent, as given.

city_overlay.title: City Overlay
city_overlay.description: The covered city whose rules were layered on, if any.

verified.title: Verified
verified.description: True when the main rule text was read verbatim at the official source.

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Where the finding is. Also accepted as a plain string ("Bedroom 2", "kitchen").

in_addition_to_refund.title: In Addition To Refund
in_addition_to_refund.description: The damages come on top of returning the amount withheld (Ohio, West Virginia), not instead of it.

estimated_max_usd.title: Estimated Max Usd
estimated_max_usd.description: fixed + multiple x basis amount (with any floor or cap); exposure, not a verdict. None when the basis is unknown (monthly rent not given).

additional.title: Additional
additional.description: City penalties in addition to the state's (not included in its estimate).

forfeits_right_to_withhold_if_late.title: Forfeits Right To Withhold If Late

Phase.title: Phase
Phase.description: Make-ready order. Values sort in sequence order via PHASE_ORDER.

PriceTier.title: PriceTier
PriceTier.description: Purchasing channel. Library prices are pm_vendor (a PM buying turns from a local vendor).

unit_type.description: Single-family homes and townhomes get house-sized defaults (floor area, locks).

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

zip.title: Zip
zip.description: The user's 5-digit US ZIP code. If it is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess, pad or correct it.

issues.title: Issues
issues.description: What was found, one plain-English item per entry, e.g. ['stained carpet in both bedrooms', 'nail holes everywhere', 'oven is filthy']. A room at the start sets the location ('Bedroom 2 carpet torn').

QuickEstimateRequest.title: QuickEstimateRequest
QuickEstimateRequest.description: Flat, primitive-only input: the easiest way to get an estimate.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: A task_id from a result line, e.g. 'carpet.clean'.

unit_price.title: Unit Price
unit_price.description: USD per uom. On a trade entry, uom 'hour' is an hourly labor rate (replaces the labor part of that trade's prices); another uom prices that trade's tasks in it.

uom.description: Unit your price is quoted in. Required with a trade unit_price. If it differs from a task's uom, the entry is not applied to that task (see rate_card_ignored).

RateCardEntry.title: RateCardEntry
RateCardEntry.description:
Your own price. Examples: {"trade": "handyman", "unit_price": 65, "uom": "hour"} (an
hourly labor rate for that trade); {"trade": "painter", "min_charge": 150} (visit minimum);
{"task_id": "carpet.clean", "unit_price": 0.2, "uom": "sq_ft"} (task_id from a result line).
A task_id entry beats a trade entry; both beat the library. The result lists what was
applied and what was ignored (rate_card_applied / rate_card_ignored).

RateWindow.title: RateWindow
RateWindow.description:
A published rate for a period (San Francisco's March-February year, a Berkeley move-out
month, a Connecticut calendar year).

unconfirmed.title: Unconfirmed
unconfirmed.description: Every triggering finding was hedged ('maybe', '?'): check first; no phase is held until the condition is confirmed (see warnings).

covered_cities.title: Covered Cities
covered_cities.description: City overlays in this state ('Name, ST').

research_notes.title: Research Notes
research_notes.description: Research notes on the rows used: where the text was read, fetch failures, renumbering, history not checked. For checking the sourcing; not warnings.

responsibility_by_finding.title: Responsibility By Finding
responsibility_by_finding.description: Set when the hint is 'mixed': the hint of each finding the line carries.

allowance.description: Quote-required lines only: a non-binding budget range. NOT included in any total; summed separately in totals.allowances.

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: summary: totals, trade scopes, every line tied to a finding (capped at 40) plus the largest must-fix/refer-out lines, a one-line note on the routine lines left out, notes, and only findings needing attention (small). full: every line, finding and source.

lines_omitted.title: Lines Omitted
lines_omitted.description: Lines left out in summary detail.

omitted_note.title: Omitted Note
omitted_note.description: Summary detail: what the omitted lines are (routine turn tasks) and their cost.

rate_card_applied.title: Rate Card Applied
rate_card_applied.description: Rate card entries that changed a price.

rate_card_ignored.title: Rate Card Ignored
rate_card_ignored.description: Rate card entries that changed nothing, with why.

ScopeResult.title: ScopeResult
ScopeResult.description:
Field order puts the answer first (summary, disclaimer, totals, refer-outs, vendor
scopes), because agents and truncating clients read from the top.

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

state.title: State
state.description: US state, 2-letter code (e.g. 'CA'); a state name also works.

city.title: City
city.description: City, for a city overlay where covered (e.g. 'Chicago'). Optional.

monthly_rent_usd.title: Monthly Rent Usd
monthly_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent, for the deposit cap check.

building_units.title: Building Units
building_units.description: Units in the building. Some interest rules depend on it (NY 6+, IL 25+).

move_in_on.title: Move In On
move_in_on.description: Tenancy start (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for interest and, when an item's age is unknown, for depreciation.

tenancy_ended_on.title: Tenancy Ended On
tenancy_ended_on.description: Lease end or termination date (YYYY-MM-DD), if different.

vacated_on.title: Vacated On
vacated_on.description: Day the tenant moved out and returned possession (YYYY-MM-DD).

forwarding_address_received_on.title: Forwarding Address Received On
forwarding_address_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's written forwarding address (YYYY-MM-DD). Several states start or hold the clock on it (Texas, Connecticut, Iowa, Minnesota).

demand_received_on.title: Demand Received On
demand_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's written demand for the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD). Arizona, Kansas, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Mississippi start the clock on it.

new_tenant_moved_in_on.title: New Tenant Moved In On
new_tenant_moved_in_on.description: Day a new tenant moved in, if the unit was re-rented (YYYY-MM-DD). West Virginia and Wisconsin can end the period earlier.

claim_notice_sent_on.title: Claim Notice Sent On
claim_notice_sent_on.description: Day you sent the written notice of intent to impose a claim on the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD). Florida: the balance is due 30 days after it.

lease_return_days.title: Lease Return Days
lease_return_days.description: Return period the lease sets, in days, where the statute lets a lease set one (Colorado up to 60, Idaho up to 30, Maine shorter).

tenant_gave_proper_notice.title: Tenant Gave Proper Notice
tenant_gave_proper_notice.description: A termination notice that meets the statute was given (Alaska: 14 days instead of 30 when nothing is deducted for damage).

contractor_needed.title: Contractor Needed
contractor_needed.description: Damage exceeds the deposit and needs a third-party contractor, and you said so in writing in time (Virginia, West Virginia: 15 more days).

deductions.title: Deductions
deductions.description: What you intend to deduct; may be empty.

documentation.description: What documentation you have; leave a field out when unknown.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: Today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the deadline status. Defaults to today (UTC); send it for repeatable results.

price_tier.description: bulk_contract (portfolio contract prices) | pm_vendor (default: a property manager buying turns from local vendors) | retail_one_off (an owner hiring one contractor).

markup_pct.title: Markup Pct
markup_pct.description: Management markup applied to every line, %.

text.title: Text
text.description: Draft itemized statement, plain text, no names or addresses.

allowed_usd.title: Allowed Usd
allowed_usd.description: Sum of lines with allowed = yes.

interest_usd.title: Interest Usd
interest_usd.description: Interest credited (0 when none or unknown).

tenant_owes_usd.title: Tenant Owes Usd
tenant_owes_usd.description: Allowed deductions above deposit + interest (collect separately).

note.title: Note
note.default: must, should and could are work lines only. visit_charges (minimum call-out and trip fees, once per trade) are added on top: subtotal = must + should + could + visit_charges; total = subtotal + tax. allowances are outside the total.

allowances.description: Budget allowance for quote-required lines (refer-outs, manual quotes). Shown outside the totals: subtotal and total never include it.
